`jobsChanged` is what a launch site or a transition calls after writing to the
registry: `ChangedMsg` to every held view, `FrameMsg` to the view on screen. The
`Update` wrapper then makes sure a chain is alive; the three are separate, and
none implies another.

This is what removes the four hand-stamped frames, and with them the failure
each of them could produce: a chain that died on the first idle tick with
nothing able to restart it, leaving the spinner frozen on the frame it died at.

#### Terminal focus (DEVDESK-210)

Bubble Tea v2 reports whether the terminal has the focus (xterm mode 1004) when
the view asks for it. The router uses it to stop the animation chain while the
terminal is blurred, and to tell the view on screen so it can skip its periodic
reads (see "Routing the level to a view").

- **Asking.** `App.View` is the only place that sets `ReportFocus`. A view's
  `View()` never does, like `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`.
- **The level.** `App.terminalBlurred` is a bool whose zero value means
  focused. `tea.BlurMsg` sets it (`handleTerminalBlur`), `tea.FocusMsg` clears
  it (`handleTerminalFocus`). Neither returns a Cmd.

content.content:
Two of those keys are worth the note. The ports table keys on the **PID, not the
socket**, so every row of a process shows the dot at once — which is what happens, the
kill takes them all. The registries table keys on the **URL**, which is the one
place D40's rule does not apply, and it does not apply because the *operation*
is host-scoped: one `docker login` really does change the answer for every entry
on that host.

`oci_resources` gathers `BusyLabels()` from **all four tabs**, not the active
one: an action started on Images goes on running after `tab`, and a spinner that
stopped turning because the user looked elsewhere would read as a hang on the
way back. Row state is drawn by the activity column and animated by the router's
`jobs.FrameMsg`; the view's own spinner turns only while a tab loads.

Deliberately outside this:

- **Scans** — they do not block the object the same way, so they are not a
  part of the status, so a footer message still wins over it.
- **A detail with a glyph suppresses the spinner:** the row's own dot already
  moves.
- **East Asian width.** `centerLine` pads by `lipgloss.Width`, which counts
  ambiguous glyphs as one cell. `View` shrinks its target width by
  `theme.StringWidth(line) - lipgloss.Width(line)` so the line is `width`
  columns for `runewidth` too.

**One constructor of sentences** (`row_activity.go`). The view fills a
`RowQuery{Runs, Failures, Context, Target, Kinds, Observed, ObservedText, Extra}`
(runs and failures of any context; they are filtered here) and calls:

- **`RowState(q)`**: the `indicator.State` for the activity column, no text.
- **`DescribeRow(q)`**: `RowActivity{State, Detail}`. Both go through
  `resolveRow`, so the glyph in the table and the sentence in the footer cannot
  disagree. The state follows `indicator.Resolve` (running > queued > failure >
  observed > idle).
The explorer reads the router's index (`shared.State.ForgeIndex`, see
`app-shell.md`) for two things.

**A level appears before the forge answers.** On opening, the roots come from
the index (`seedFromIndex`); on `→`, a group's children do (`indexedLevel`). The
level is then read from the forge anyway, decorated, **behind** what is shown
(`refreshLevel`): the table keeps its rows, the breadcrumb and the shortcuts,
and the footer says `Updating from GitLab...` with the spinner. Only a level the
index does not know waits on the forge, as every level used to.

- **The answer is laid over, not swapped in** (`mergeLevel`). A node that stayed
  keeps its pointer — its children, its place in the navigation stack if the user
  is inside it — and takes the forge's fields; one that went is dropped; the
  cursor stays on the same path. Swapping the slice would have orphaned a path
  the user had already drilled through.
- **`TreeNode.Fresh`** says a level came from the forge in this session. A level
  that is not fresh is read again when shown; one that is, is not.
- **The index is corrected by what is shown.** Each decorated answer replaces its
  level in the index (`ReplaceLevel`), creates add to it (`With`), deletes remove
  a subtree (`Without`) — so `g` stops offering what the user has already seen
  gone, without waiting for the next walk.
- **An answer older than a create or a delete is discarded.** Creating and
  deleting are allowed while a level refreshes behind the index — nothing blocks
registry's dot instead. `explorerRow.Activity` is stamped by `rowsFor` from
`rowState`, which reads `components.DescribeRow` over the `ChangedMsg` copies
(`Runs`, `Failures`, `Context`; Rule 110). The blink phase is read by the table
at render: `handleFrameMsg` calls `SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)` and rebuilds no
row. The first-load and refresh spinners in the footer are unchanged.

Which kinds a row answers for (`rowKinds`):
### The clone is a run of the registry (§3.58, D3)

`cloneList` used to hold five states, a slice of rows, an index keyed on the
path and a spinner frame of its own. That was the fifth bookkeeping beside the
four `internal/jobs` replaced — and the one the plan named as the prototype to
generalise, because it was already a jobs view for a single kind.

### A loading table stays a table

When a table-backed view is loading data, the *table itself* stays on screen — with its header and columns — and the loading indication is a `Status` in the footer, with a spinner. A body that swapped itself out for a spinner while loading would visibly lose its header and columns for the duration of every refresh, then regain them — a layout jump on every single reload. As a direct consequence, an "empty" message like "No images found" is only shown once loading has actually finished; otherwise the table would be announcing the absence of results it hasn't even finished looking for yet.

## Tables: one shared mechanism for width, sorting, and filtering
**Stopping work has two distinct scopes**, and both are exposed as separate keys where applicable: cancelling a *run* stops the queue (nothing further starts; anything still queued is marked skipped), while cancelling a *target* interrupts one piece of work already running. Not every kind of work can be safely interrupted mid-flight — a delete request already sent to a forge can't be un-sent — so the registry tracks per-kind whether cancellation-in-flight is even offered.

### One spinner, broadcast everywhere

Views never hold a pointer into the registry. The router hands out a read-only snapshot via `jobs.ChangedMsg`, broadcast to every held view (on screen or not) whenever anything changes — so navigating back to a view that missed some progress shows the current state without it having to ask. There is exactly one spinner tick chain for the whole application, owned by the router, identified by a sequence number so a stale tick from a superseded chain is simply dropped.

13	## Critical rules (summary)
14	
15	**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.
16	
17	**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.
18	
19	**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with `Spinner` + `SetSpinnerFrame` for a view's own loading, with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`) for work the router tracks. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.
20	
21	**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.
22	
23	**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.
24	
25	**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.
26	
27	**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.
